what_worked: Tier-escalation cohort on slide 7 and risk/opportunity pairing on slide 5 show genuine analytical structure.
fix_next: Ground every metric in the actual dataset field (30-day revenue, not MRR/ARR) and disclose missingness and zero-revenue rows.
verdict: Polished template masks fabricated MRR framing and unverifiable numbers throughout.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1: Total revenue called '$13.47M MRR' but reference is $15.6M 30-day revenue; '$161.7M ARR' fabricated by annualizing wrong base; top-10 share stated 48.0% vs reference 49.6%. Slide 2: '$133.8M L12M realized' and '$161.7M forward ARR' have no dataset basis; +64.4% SaaS 30D growth unverifiable. Slide 3: B2B avg $13,150 and B2C avg $5,102 labeled 'Avg MRR' but field is not MRR; segment totals ($3.35M B2B, $2.05M B2C) don't reconcile to portfolio total. Slide 4: AI '$1.81M MRR' vs reference $2.36M total; SaaS '$588.7k' vs reference $703.5k; Marketing '$444.5k' vs reference $1.32M. Slide 5: 26.5% single-asset share unverifiable. Slide 7: tier percentages sum to ~100.1% but individual figures not independently checkable.

evidence.insight: Mid-tier scaling thesis (slide 7) and concentration risk (slide 5) are analytically sound ideas, but rest on fabricated MRR framing rather than actual 30-day revenue, limiting decision-usefulness.
evidence.narrative: Logical flow from snapshot through growth, unit economics, drivers, risks, memo, and cohorts. But the throughline is an investment-committee pitch whose entire foundation (MRR/ARR) is unsupported by the dataset.
evidence.framing: Deck never names the dataset, its source, or its limitations. 274 missing categories, 288 missing audience_type, 216 zero-revenue rows all unmentioned. 'Investment Committee Briefing' framing is clear but scope and definitions are absent for a cold reader.
evidence.accuracy: Core error: dataset field is 30-day revenue, not MRR. All ARR figures are therefore fabricated. Multiple category totals contradict reference (Marketing $444.5k vs $1.32M). Top-10 share 48.0% vs 49.6%. B2B/B2C means presented without median context or outlier caveat.
evidence.visual: Clean card-based layout with consistent typography and restrained palette. But only slide 7 has any data visualization (horizontal bars without axis labels). Six slides are text-only cards with heavy whitespace. No scatter plots, distributions, or annotated charts anywhere.
evidence.ai_slop: Every slide uses identical card-plus-bottom-callout template. Consulting jargon throughout: 'Power-Law Portfolio,' 'Revenue Cohort Architecture,' 'Strategic Balance Sheet,' 'Freemium Conversion Chasm.' Decorative emoji-icons add no analytical value. Framing feels templated, not data-earned.

change_reason: Lowered framing from 4.5 to 4.0: complete absence of dataset provenance, missingness disclosure, and zero-revenue acknowledgment is more severe than preliminary suggested. All other scores confirmed after independent review.
